title: Quantum computers
summary: Build two-qubit circuits: superposition, interference and entanglement, and where qubits could help.

ideas.how: error correction spreads one reliable qubit over many noisy ones
qubits compute with superposition and interference

then: Quantum computing is an idea (Feynman, 1982); Shor's factoring algorithm arrives in 1994.
Labs build machines with a handful to dozens of qubits.
Google claims quantum supremacy (2019) on a 53-qubit chip; error rates are still too high for useful work.
Error correction starts to work: logical qubits beat physical ones.
Plans: error-corrected machines are scaled up for the first useful applications.
Plans: fault-tolerant quantum computers from IBM and Quantinuum, targeted for 2029.

challenges.title: One look, no luck
challenges.task: A prize hides in one of four boxes. Make it impossible for one look to miss.
challenges.hint: Try Flip, then Mirror, then Look. Watch the squares move across the average line.
challenges.why: Flip marks the prize without showing it, and Mirror turns that small mark into a big difference. With four boxes one step cancels every wrong box exactly, so nothing had to be checked one by one.

challenges.title: One step too many
challenges.task: With 8 boxes, grow the prize square as far as it goes, then take one more step. What happens?
challenges.hint: Press Flip then Mirror, and watch the prize square after each pair.
challenges.why: The steps rotate the state past the answer, so the chance rises, peaks and falls again. A quantum search has to stop at the right moment, which is why it matters how many answers there are.

challenges.title: Clean enough for a million
challenges.task: A search of about a million boxes takes about 800 steps. Lower the noise until it finds the prize half the time.
challenges.hint: Move the noise slider down and watch the best chance for a million boxes.
challenges.why: Noise adds up over every step, so a long search needs each step to be better than about 0.1% wrong. That is why error correction comes first: spending many raw qubits to make one reliable one.

challenges.title: Entangle two qubits
challenges.task: Build circuits for certainty, interference and entanglement.
